   "source": [
    "## 🔍 What is a Stored Procedure?\n",
    "A stored procedure is a saved collection of SQL statements that you can execute as a single unit. \n",
    "Think of it like a reusable script that performs a specific task—such as generating a report, aggregating data, or transforming datasets."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9ae5db85",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 💡 How Stored Procedures Help in Data Analytics\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "1) Encapsulation of Logic\n",
    "You can encapsulate complex business logic (joins, filters, aggregations) into a stored procedure.  \n",
    "This makes your analytics workflows cleaner and easier to maintain.  \n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "2) Parameterization\n",
    "Stored procedures can accept parameters, allowing analysts to run the same report for different time periods, departments, or other filters.  \n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "3) Performance Optimization\n",
    "SQL Server caches execution plans for stored procedures, which can improve performance compared to ad-hoc queries.  \n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "4) Security and Access Control\n",
    "You can grant users permission to execute a stored procedure without giving them direct access to the underlying tables.  \n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "5) Automation\n",
    "Stored procedures can be scheduled to run automatically (e.g., nightly reports), making them ideal for recurring analytics tasks."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "54cbd2f5",
   "metadata": {
    "vscode": {
     "languageId": "polyglot-notebook"
